_comment: Errors check_protocol_compatibility.py is told to accept, enumerated one
by one rather than suppressed wholesale.
The Runtime domain was declared in v8's js_protocol.pdl, which upstream
passes to this check alongside browser_protocol.pdl. V8 is deleted and v8/
was a git submodule, so js_protocol.pdl cannot be recovered from this
repository even as a data file.
The live domains no longer mention Runtime at all: the scalar aliases
(ScriptId, RemoteObjectId, ExecutionContextId, Timestamp) were inlined to
the primitives they aliased, which changes nothing on the wire, and the
object types (RemoteObject, StackTrace) were removed along with the
commands that could not work without them.
What still refers to Runtime is browser_protocol-1.3.json, the frozen 1.3
baseline this check compares against. It describes a protocol that had a
script engine behind it. Every entry below is that baseline naming a type
this build intentionally no longer has. Listing them keeps the check doing
its real job -- catching an unintended change to a domain that still
errors: Can not resolve type: Runtime.ExecutionContextId
Can not resolve type: Runtime.RemoteObjectId
Can not resolve type: Runtime.ScriptId
Can not resolve type: Runtime.Timestamp
Can not resolve type: Runtime.StackTrace
Can not resolve type: Runtime.RemoteObject
